title: Vialling of Label-Free GAG Disaccharide Standards and Samples for HILIC-MS/MS Analysis
author: H Davies-Strickleton
materials: In a preceding protocol, Equimolar Stock Solutions were prepared in water. Here, these are diluted 1 in 20 in Standard Diluent to prepare Equimolar Disaccharide Standards for subsequent HILIC-MS/MS analysis . ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Rationale of 50 nM Equimolar Disaccharide Standard preparation In this section, an 50 nM Equimolar Disaccharide Standard (a mixture of disaccharide standards at equal molar concentration) is prepared for HILIC-MS/MS injection and analysis. The purpose of this 50 nM Equimolar Disaccharide Standard is to correct for disaccharide specific variability in analysis and to provide a single point calibration for the approximation of disaccharide amount (semi-quantification). The semi-quantification presented here is appropriate for the relative quantification of disaccharide amounts, total GAG amounts (by summation of disaccharide amounts) and disaccharide composition (relative ratio of disaccharides compared to total GAG). (For comparison of relative amounts of disaccharides in samples, without disaccharide composition, standard preparation may not be required.) Rationale of 5, 500 and 5000 nM Equimolar Disaccharide Linearity Standard preparation Optional 5, 500 and 5000 nM Equimolar Disaccharide Linearity Standards may also be prepared. These serve as (a) test injections to optimise LC-MS conditions prior to analysis and/or (b) to confirm analyte linearity. Rationale of Internal Standard addition to Standard Diluent The Equimolar Disaccharide Standard is spiked with an Internal Standard, to correct for variability in instrument performance. In a separate protocol for preparation of GAG disaccharides from biological tissues , samples were also spiked with the Internal Standard.

Internal Standard The internal standard solutions may have been prepared during the sample preparation protocol , and may be used within one week of prep if kept at 4 °C . The internal standard stock is stored at -20 o C in 10 µL aliquots of 1 mg/mL in ddH 2 O.

steps.title: Prepare 250 mM Ammonium Acetate Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare approximately 1 L of 250 mM Ammonium Acetate Stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 19.27 g Ammonium acetate (VWR International Catalog #84885.180).
Add to 1 L ddH2O (or calculate volume V = m / (C*MW) where m is mass, C=0.25, and MW=77.08).
Mix well.
Store for up to one year at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Solution A
steps.instruction: Prepare Solution A (77% acetonitrile, 45 mM ammonium acetate). For 100 mL, use a measuring cylinder to add the following to a duran bottle:

substeps.instruction: Add 77 mL Acetonitrile LC-MS Grade (Fisher Scientific Catalog #A/0638/15).
Add 18 mL 250 mM Ammonium Acetate Stock.
Add 5 mL ddH2O.
Mix well and allow to reach room temperature.
Store at room temperature for up to 3 months.

steps.title: Prepare Internal Standard Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of internal standard dilutions from the 1 mg/mL stock (Iduron Catalog #HD009).

substeps.instruction: Thaw the 1 mg/mL Internal Standard Stock ∆UA-2S GlcNCOEt-6S (I-P).
Prepare a 10 μg/mL solution: add 10 µL aliquot of stock to 990 µL ddH2O and mix well.
Prepare a 1 μg/mL solution: add 100 µL of the 10 μg/mL solution to 900 µL ddH2O, mix well, and store at 4 °C when not in use.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Diluent
steps.instruction: Prepare Sample Diluent (93 parts Solution A, 2 parts ddH2O) in a 30 mL glass vial (WHEATON Z550981). Prepare on the day of use.

substeps.instruction: Add 6324 µL Solution A (equilibrate pipette tip by withdrawing liquid slowly up and down).
Add 136 µL ddH2O.
Mix well.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Diluent
steps.instruction: Prepare Standard Diluent (93 parts Solution A, 2 parts 1 μg/mL internal standard) in a glass HPLC vial. Prepare on the day of use.

substeps.instruction: Add 930 µL Solution A (equilibrate pipette tip by withdrawing liquid slowly up and down).
Add 20 µL 1 μg/mL Internal Standard Solution.
Mix well.

steps.title: Prepare Blank Vials
steps.instruction: Prepare Blank Diluent and Blank Internal Standard vials using HPLC insert vials.

substeps.instruction: Blank Diluent: Add 60 µL Solution A.
Blank Internal Standard: Add 57 µL Standard Diluent (equilibrate pipette tip first) and 3 µL water; mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Reconstitute GAG Disaccharide Samples
steps.instruction: Reconstitute lyophilized GAG disaccharides from biological tissues.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL ddH2O to the freeze-dried sample.
Solubilize at room temperature for at least 10 minutes.
Vortex briefly.
Centrifuge at 15,000 rpm for 5 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Dilute Samples for Analysis
steps.instruction: Dilute samples 1 in 20 using Sample Diluent in Certified QSertVial™ (Supelco 29391-U) HPLC insert vials.

substeps.instruction: Add 57 µL Sample Diluent (equilibrate pipette tip first).
Add 3 µL sample supernatant.
Mix well by pipetting.
If precipitate is visible, transfer to microfuge tubes, centrifuge at 15,000 rpm for 10 minutes, and transfer supernatant to fresh HPLC insert vials.

steps.title: Prepare Equimolar Disaccharide Standards
steps.instruction: Dilute Equimolar Stock Solutions 1 in 20 using Standard Diluent in Certified QSertVial™ (Supelco 29391-U) HPLC insert vials.

substeps.instruction: Label vials according to the desired concentration (5, 50, 500, or 5000 nM).
Add 57 µL Standard Diluent (equilibrate pipette tip first).
Add 3 µL of the corresponding Equimolar Stock Solution (e.g., 1 µM stock for 50 nM standard, 100 µM stock for 5000 nM standard, 10 µM stock for 500 nM standard, or 0.1 µM stock for 5 nM standard).
Mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Equilibrate Vials in Autosampler
steps.instruction: Place all prepared vials in the autosampler 90 minutes before injection to equilibrate to the autosampler temperature.

substeps.instruction: Include Blank Diluent, Blank Internal Standard, Equimolar Disaccharide Standards (50 nM and optional 5, 500, 5000 nM), Test Samples, and Positive Control Sample.
